attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, published under his name.

semantics.note: Captures the exemption part of the sentence and correctly leaves out the revenue aside and the 'revolve around' rhetoric. It is a present-tense description of big tech's stated objective, so observation is the right kind.

contract.note: Reading 'any regulation' as a blanket exemption is the ordinary meaning of what Marcus wrote. The context (EU AI Act foundation-model talks) allows a narrower, hyperbolic reading, and the contract flags this. The result depends on taking his literal scope.

evidence.note: Google's policy paper of 14 Nov 2023, inside the target period, explicitly calls for regulating AI and makes substantive recommendations. It is a company disclosure, but it is direct evidence of a stated policy aim, which is what the claim is about.

23 Nov 2023 industry statement lobbying to limit foundation-model duties to transparency standards. This fits the narrower concern, but it accepts some rules and backs regulating high-risk uses, so it does not show a push to escape all regulation.

reviews.rationale: On the plain reading, the claim is that big tech wanted generative AI exempt from all binding regulation. In November 2023 Google publicly called for AI regulation with substantive rules (e1). The main industry lobbying (e2) sought narrower foundation-model duties, not a blanket exemption. Lobbying to weaken the foundation-model rules is real, but the blanket claim as written is contradicted.
